root_cause.summary: v029_progress() never attached band_flow or gate_distance to its return value, while the final-report transform printed report['progress']['gate_distance'] and ['band_flow'].
how_it_got_there: Both helper functions were defined and both print statements were installed.
The edit that would have attached them to v029_progress()'s return dict lived in the same patch script as a second edit whose assertion failed ('promotion print transform not found').
That assertion aborted the script before it wrote the file, so the return-value edit was discarded along with it.
The follow-up patch fixed only the assertion that had errored and did not re-apply the discarded edit.
This is my error, not a defect in the scaffold.
why_the_tests_missed_it: test_v029_band_flow_reconstructs_the_v028_transitions and test_v029_gate_distance_... call the helpers directly.
test_v029_transform_targets_exist_and_runtime_compiles asserts the print strings appear in the runtime source.
No test connected the two: nothing asserted that the dict v029_progress returns contains the keys the reporter reads from it.

evidence: In the transformed runtime, best.pt, latest.pt, the evaluation report and run-state.json upload at lines 1003-1015.
The failing print is at line 1020, after every upload.
run-state.json therefore carries status evaluation_complete and the run_id, so v0.0.30 resolves the v0.0.29 source normally.

findings.claim: Both legacy gates now pass, and the remaining promotion distance is about one and a half runs at the observed rate.
evidence: Legacy exact copy 6/9 clears 0.5556; legacy continuation 65/69 = 0.9420 clears 0.90.
Expanded exact copy needs 36/90 and stands at 32/90: four cases.
Expanded continuation needs 657/730 and stands at 642/730: fifteen tokens.
v0.0.28 delivered +33 continuation tokens, v0.0.29 delivered +10.

findings.claim: The two remaining gates are consistent rather than competing, so one improvement satisfies both.
evidence: 0.40 exact copy under independent errors needs per-token 0.89318, which is 652/730.
The 0.90 continuation gate is 657/730, five tokens beyond that.

findings.claim: The k = 2 worst-position statistic still matches the data, so the objective does not need changing.
evidence: 730 x (1 - 0.8795) = 88.0 wrong continuation decisions over 58 failing rows is 1.52 each.
Adding the three first-token failures gives 1.57 wrong decisions per failing row, against 1.66 when k = 2 was chosen.

findings.claim: More steps at this schedule would not have helped; the run had already peaked.
evidence: The selected best checkpoint was step 479 of 600, so the final 120 steps produced nothing better.
The cosine schedule is near its floor by then.
findings.consequence: The gain has to come from continuing at a fresh schedule from the new checkpoint, which is exactly what v0.0.30 does. Step count stays at 600.

recommended_next_phase.strategy: same objective, v0.0.29 source, reporter repaired
notes: Attach band_flow and gate_distance to the progress result, which is the one-line fix.
Read the trailing diagnostic prints defensively, so a reporting defect can never again fail a run whose artifacts are already uploaded.
Add a contract test that derives the required keys from the transform text itself and checks the producing functions supply them, so this class of drift cannot recur silently.
Change nothing else. k = 2 still matches the measured failure count, both legacy gates pass, and the remaining distance is fifteen token decisions.
